key_insight: Retention-constrained fine-tuning improves an aluminium MACE potential’s defect predictions while preserving its tested near-equilibrium mechanical and vibrational response.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports atomistic simulations of plasticity with better defect energetics and stresses without sacrificing validated bulk behavior.
method: Select configurations using conditional force uncertainty, with within-batch covariance updates.
Iteratively update all model parameters while anchoring historical relative energies.
Gate updates against historical elastic-group energy and vibrational tolerances.
evidence_signal: After 32 acquired configurations and 400 gradient updates, mean development force error fell from 22.43 to 21.52 meV/Å, outperforming sampling baselines; all three force-uncertainty runs met retention criteria, with harmonic phonon RMS drift below 0.05 THz.
watch_item: Retention is demonstrated for tested aluminium benchmarks; new deformation regimes require additional validation and compatible reference-energy protocols.
paper_title: Retention-constrained fine-tuning of a pre-trained aluminium MACE potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity
